protocol.optimizer: coarse-to-fine L-BFGS (RobustExtractor), strong-Wolfe, history 50, max 300 iterations per stage
protocol.scaling: n = n0 + 0.1 x, kappa = kappa0 + 0.005 x, d = d0 exp(0.1 x)
protocol.start_box: n ± 0.5, kappa ± 0.01 (clipped >= 0), d x [0.5, 1.5] around the true values

data.sigma_window: first 10 ps of the sample trace

secondary_minima.criterion: rMSE more than 0.5 % above the best of the eight starts

C14_noise_table.description: pre-pulse noise of the six measured traces; white = std(first difference)/sqrt(2) per 2-ps segment (min = quietest segment); ACF of the demeaned 0-10 ps window

C1_PI_model_variants.description: PI/Si refit, same 8 starts and coarse-to-fine L-BFGS as loop 0; rmse_over_sigma uses sigma of the PI sample trace (R12)

a_cramer_rao.description: CR 1-sigma bounds of the film parameters at the true values (sweep geometry, sigma of the reference pre-pulse, white noise, exact model); for an efficient unbiased estimator the median |error| is 0.674 x CR

b_ten_draws.description: 10 additional noise draws (seeds 50000+1000 i+draw) at 5-20 um, 5 starts each, best start re-polished with full-band L-BFGS (1500 iterations, tolerances 1e-12); errors after polish

fig2b_variant.reason: lower rMSE of C1 variants (b) and (c)

pi_2511.description: polyimide on HR Si, re-measured 2026-11-25 as a reference-sample-reference bracket (10 000 waveforms each)
pi_2511.sigma_window: first 10 ps of the 2026-11-25 sample trace (R12)

data_checks.sign_convention: delays and tau positive = sample later than reference

n_Si_without_tau.definition: physical = literature value inside the n_Si range of the no-tau fits against ref1 and ref2 (the timing bracket) and |n_Si/3.4175 - 1| < 1 %

pi_2511.verdict: BETTER. The bracket measures a time-zero drift of +40.0 fs in 38 min (ref2 - ref1, phase slope 0.2-2 THz; main peak +40.7 fs). Against the mean reference the paper protocol (six parameters, no tau) gives n_Si = 3.4018 (-0.46 % vs 3.4175; old pair 3.2592, -4.6 %), equivalent to a -6.6 fs time-zero error; 3.4175 lies between the ref1 and ref2 fits (3.4506 / 3.3551); rMSE 2.23 sigma vs 2.69 sigma. With tau, a free tau = -5.1 fs (n_Si fixed) / -1.2 fs (all free) against the mean reference, inside the measured drift, instead of -65 / -70 fs; the single-reference taus differ by 38.9 fs, i.e. the fit sees the measured drift. Not improved: d_PI moves further from the profilometer (26.42 vs 25.84 um without tau; 25.55 vs 25.25 um with n_Si fixed + tau, a), n*d_PI rises to 46.28 um (old 44.26), fewer starts agree without tau (2/8 vs 6/8), and the best tau, a misfit is 1.90 sigma vs 1.70 sigma. The free tau is no longer needed; the remaining tau, a gain comes from the amplitude (a = 1.014; ref2/ref1 = 1.010).
